summary: Ciclopirox Topical Solution 8% is a nail lacquer indicated, as part of a comprehensive management program, for mild-to-moderate onychomycosis of the fingernails and toenails without lunula involvement due to Trichophyton rubrum in immunocompetent patients. The program requires daily application, weekly removal with alcohol and patient nail trimming, and periodic (as often as monthly) professional removal of unattached infected nail. Treatment may be needed for up to 48 weeks, complete cure rates are low (under 12% achieved a clear or almost clear nail), and the product is flammable.
indications: Mild to moderate onychomycosis of fingernails and toenails without lunula involvement due to Trichophyton rubrum, in immunocompetent patients, as a component of a comprehensive management program

dosage.d: Apply 8% solution evenly over the entire nail plate and 5 mm of surrounding skin; if possible to the nail bed, hyponychium, and under-surface of the nail plate
dosage.t: Once daily, preferably at bedtime (or 8 hours before washing)
dosage.n: Apply over previous coat; remove all coats with alcohol every 7 days, then file/trim, then restart cycle. Treat up to 48 weeks
Considered safe based on adult safety profile; no pediatric clinical trials conducted

admin: Apply once daily to all affected nails with the applicator brush, evenly over the entire nail plate plus 5 mm of surrounding skin
Do not remove daily applications; apply each new coat over the prior coat
Every 7 days, remove all lacquer with alcohol, then file loose nail material and trim nails
Professional removal of unattached, infected nail as often as monthly is an integral part of therapy
For external use on nails and immediately adjacent skin only; avoid eyes and mucous membranes
Avoid use near heat or open flame because the product is flammable; do not use nail polish or cosmetics on treated nails
moa: Ciclopirox is a hydroxypyridone antifungal. One in vitro study suggests it acts by chelating polyvalent cations (Fe3+ or Al3+), inhibiting the metal-dependent fungal enzymes that degrade peroxides within the fungal cell; the clinical significance of this finding is not fully established.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to ciclopirox or any component of the formulation
relative: Insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus or diabetic neuropathy (risk from nail removal/trimming; no relevant clinical experience)
monitor: Application-site irritation (redness, itching, burning, blistering, swelling, oozing)
Signs of sensitization or chemical irritation

preg: Pregnancy Category B. Animal teratology studies (oral and topical) in mice, rats, rabbits, and monkeys did not show significant fetal malformations. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether ciclopirox is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: No dosage adjustment provided in labeling; systemic absorption from the nail lacquer is minimal (mean absorption less than 5% of the applied dose). Ciclopirox is eliminated mainly renally as glucuronide after systemic exposure.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment provided in labeling; systemic absorption is minimal.

moderate: Systemic antifungal agents for onychomycosis: concomitant use is not recommended (effect on their efficacy not studied)
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol is used to remove the lacquer weekly; the product itself is flammable and must be kept away from heat and open flame.

common: Erythema of the proximal nail fold
Mild, transient irritation of surrounding skin
rare: Nail shape change, ingrown toenail, nail discoloration

Nail response (improvement may take ~6 months; full course up to 48 weeks)

pk: Slow; initial improvement may take ~6 months of therapy
Mean maximal serum level ~31 ng/mL after 2 months of daily use; absorption <5% of applied dose

pearls: Effective only for mild-to-moderate disease without lunula involvement; cure rates are low (under 12% clear/almost clear in trials)
Success depends on the full program: daily lacquer, weekly alcohol removal and trimming, and periodic professional debridement

missed: If a daily application is missed, apply it as soon as remembered and continue the once-daily schedule; do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose. Maintaining the daily routine and the weekly alcohol-removal cycle is important for benefit.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical nail use given minimal systemic absorption. The product is for external use only and is not for ophthalmic, oral, or intravaginal use; in case of accidental ingestion or eye contact, provide supportive care and rinse/flush as appropriate.
